Preface
We usually divide the history of the philosophical world into periodsâ€”an-
cient, medieval, and modernâ€”and teach modern philosophy beginning with
RenÃ© Descartes and ending with Immanuel Kant.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: The reason for this typical- ly involves a view of modern philosophy as consisting of two distinct camps: continental rationalists (Descartes, Baruch Spinoza, and Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz), who it is said emphasize reason at the expense of the senses, and British empiricists (John Locke, George Berkeley, and David Hume), who accentuate the senses after rejecting innate ideas.
text_raw:
The reason for this typical-
ly involves a view of modern philosophy as consisting of two distinct camps:
continental rationalists (Descartes, Baruch Spinoza, and Gottfried Wilhelm
Leibniz), who it is said emphasize reason at the expense of the senses, and
British empiricists (John Locke, George Berkeley, and David Hume), who
accentuate the senses after rejecting innate ideas.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: As we teach him, Des- cartes, â€œthe father of modern philosophy,â€ breaks with Scholasticism and medieval philosophy by calling all beliefs into doubt (especially those based on the senses); he seeks to ground all knowledge on the innate ideas he discovers within himself and then reflects upon, beginning with the one he has of himself as a thinking thing (in the cogito).
text_raw:
As we teach him, Des-
cartes, â€œthe father of modern philosophy,â€ breaks with Scholasticism and
medieval philosophy by calling all beliefs into doubt (especially those based
on the senses); he seeks to ground all knowledge on the innate ideas he
discovers within himself and then reflects upon, beginning with the one he
has of himself as a thinking thing (in the cogito).

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: The other rationalists follow, trying to come to a clear and distinct conception of their own ideas and to establish knowledge about the world with the same kind of absolute certainty and necessity attainable in mathematics.
text_raw:
The other rationalists
follow, trying to come to a clear and distinct conception of their own ideas
and to establish knowledge about the world with the same kind of absolute
certainty and necessity attainable in mathematics.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: Locke and the empiricists, in turn, break with the rationalists by rejecting innate ideas, claiming instead that the content of all of our mental states stems from experience, whether through sensation or reflection.
text_raw:
Locke and the empiricists,
in turn, break with the rationalists by rejecting innate ideas, claiming instead
that the content of all of our mental states stems from experience, whether
through sensation or reflection.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: The proper task of philosophy becomes ana- lyzing the meaning of the ideas we receive from sensation and reflection and determining what we can come to know about the world on that basis.
text_raw:
The proper task of philosophy becomes ana-
lyzing the meaning of the ideas we receive from sensation and reflection and
determining what we can come to know about the world on that basis.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: Given this picture, Kant is then presented as the culminating figure of modern philosophy because of his attempt to synthesize the rationalist and empiricist traditions.
